title: Implement monotonic tone LUT via CDF histogram specification
description: Create `src/lumamatch/tonemap.py` with `build_lut`, the core of the tool. Given the target image's L* histogram and the reference image's L* histogram, produce the monotonic tone curve that minimizes EMD between the mapped target and the reference. In one dimension the optimal transport map under any convex cost is the monotone rearrangement T = F_ref^-1 . F_src, so classic CDF-based histogram specification IS the EMD minimizer over monotonic maps — the answer is closed-form, exact, and requires no search.
acceptanceCriteria: `build_lut(src_counts, ref_counts, edges) -> np.ndarray` returns float64 of length `len(src_counts)`
The returned LUT is non-decreasing: `np.all(np.diff(lut) >= 0)` holds for every input, including adversarial ones
Identity case: when `src_counts == ref_counts`, the LUT is within 0.5 L* of the bin centers (an approximate identity map)
Applying the LUT to the source reduces EMD to near zero for any monotonic distortion of the same underlying distribution
A degenerate source (all mass in one bin) produces a valid non-decreasing LUT without NaN or inf
A degenerate reference (all mass in one bin) maps everything to approximately that bin's L* value
No NaN or inf appears in the output for any of the tested inputs
Unit tests cover all the above; `ruff check` clean

steps.details: Import `to_pmf`, `bin_centers` from `histogram.py`. Validate `src_counts.shape == ref_counts.shape` and `len(edges) == len(src_counts) + 1`, raising `ValueError` naming the actual lengths.

`src_cdf = np.cumsum(to_pmf(src_counts))` and `ref_cdf = np.cumsum(to_pmf(ref_counts))`. Both are non-decreasing and end at 1.0. Force the last element of each to exactly 1.0 to remove floating-point cumsum drift, which otherwise makes the top of the interpolation range slightly unreachable.

steps.description: Invert the reference CDF by interpolation
steps.details: The target L* for source bin i is the L* where ref_cdf reaches src_cdf[i]. Because ref_cdf is monotone non-decreasing, use `np.interp(src_cdf, ref_cdf, centers)` where `centers = bin_centers(edges)` — np.interp requires its xp argument to be non-decreasing, which ref_cdf is by construction. This yields one output L* per source bin.

Where ref_cdf is flat (empty reference bins), np.interp returns the first matching x, which biases mapped values toward the low end of a plateau. Document this in a block comment: it is the correct monotone choice (the left-continuous inverse) and keeps the map non-decreasing. Do not attempt to average across plateaus — that can break monotonicity.

Apply `lut = np.maximum.accumulate(lut)` then `lut = np.clip(lut, L_MIN, L_MAX)`. Both are defensive: the interpolation should already be monotone, but this makes the guarantee unconditional and cheap. Add a comment saying this is the hard guarantee that pixel ordering is preserved, which is a stated product requirement.

Write `assert_monotonic(lut) -> None` raising `ValueError` if `np.any(np.diff(lut) < 0)` or if `not np.all(np.isfinite(lut))`. Call it at the end of `build_lut` so a violation can never escape into the pipeline, and reuse it from the tests.

Create `tests/test_tonemap_lut.py`: (a) identity case — same histogram in and out, LUT within 0.5 of bin centers; (b) monotonicity over 50 seeded random histogram pairs; (c) finiteness over the same 50 pairs; (d) degenerate source (single spike) yields a valid non-decreasing LUT; (e) degenerate reference (single spike at bin 100) maps all bins to approximately that L*; (f) all values in [0,100]; (g) ValueError on mismatched lengths.
Run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q` and `.venv/bin/ruff check src tests`. Record in LOG.md that the LUT is closed-form optimal, not iterative.

technicalNotes: The original requirements sketched a greedy dark-to-light bin walk. That is a discrete approximation of exactly this CDF inverse; the interpolated CDF form is the exact version and is both simpler and faster. Do not implement the greedy variant.

np.interp requires xp non-decreasing. ref_cdf satisfies this. If you ever swap the argument order you will get silent garbage rather than an error — the test suite's monotonicity and identity checks are the guard.
Forcing cdf[-1] = 1.0 matters: cumsum of a PMF can land at 0.9999999999999998, which makes the brightest source bin interpolate short of the reference maximum and leaves a small systematic EMD floor.
An exact histogram match is generally impossible under a monotonic constraint — that is inherent, not a bug. The test tolerance in TASK-21 is relative (>=95% EMD reduction) for this reason.
Keep this module focused on the LUT; application to pixels is TASK-12.
